assumptions: The format has an arbitrary integer radix beta >= 2, positive precision p, and an inclusive finite exponent interval [emin, emax].
Representability is exactly equation (1): x=m*beta^e for integer m and e with -beta^p<m<beta^p and emin<=e<=emax; representations need not be normalized or unique.
Both ordered inputs x and y belong to the same floating-point set F.
Some permitted representation of x satisfies condition (7), |y| <= (beta^p-beta/2)*beta^e(x).
FastTwoSum executes one nearest addition followed by two faithful subtractions, with no fixed tie rule.
The exact sum and both exact subtraction results are within the nonoverflow range required by equation (8); representability and exact subtraction are conclusions of the radix argument, not premises.
The real-valued set model has no infinities, NaNs, exception flags, or signed-zero distinction, and Theorem 2 states no separate underflow exclusion.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p12_t2_fast_two_sum_exact (fmt : P12RadixFormat) (x y : Real) (tr : P12FastTwoSumTrace) (hx : p12Representable fmt x) (hy : p12Representable fmt y) (hcondition7 : exists rx : P12Representation fmt x, abs y <= (fmt.mantissaBound-fmt.betaR/2)*fmt.scale rx.exponent) (run : P12FastTwoSumExecution fmt x y tr) : tr.t=tr.s-x and tr.e=y-tr.t and tr.s+tr.e=x+y and abs(tr.s-(x+y))<=abs y
formal_statement.plain_language: For equation-(1) floating-point inputs satisfying condition (7), original FastTwoSum with nearest addition and faithful subtraction computes both subtractions exactly and returns an exact two-term transform.

informal_proof: Choose the condition-(7) representation of x and rebase y so e(y)<=e(x). Follow Theorem 2's equal-exponent, exact-addition, and complementary large-sum cases to prove the equation-(8) bound for s-x, making t=s-x by faithful rounding. Nearest addition gives |s-(x+y)|<=|y|; the derived exponent of t then gives the equation-(8) bound for y-t, so e=y-t. Exact algebra yields s+e=x+y.
informal_statement: Theorem 2 for arbitrary radix: equation-(1) inputs satisfying the existential threshold (7) make the original nearest-addition/faithful-subtraction FastTwoSum transform error-free, with both subtraction identities and equation (10)'s local error bound exposed.
